item.description: - **Col on Windows and Linux**: the island comes to Windows 10 and 11 and to Linux as a preview, as native apps built for each system (C# and WPF on Windows; Vala, GTK 4 and libadwaita on Linux), not a web view. A floating pill at the top of the screen shows what plays with its synced lyrics, your volume and battery, a timer, your clipboard, and Claude Code and Codex with Allow and Deny, through the same `colctl` command, API and hooks as on the Mac. On Linux it is a layer-shell overlay on KDE Plasma, COSMIC, Hyprland, Sway and niri, and runs under XWayland on GNOME. Download the Windows installer or zips, or the Linux `.deb` packages and tarballs, from the release. The Windows builds are not signed yet: SmartScreen asks once. - **Eleven languages**: Col now speaks German, Dutch, Italian, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese, besides English and French, and follows the language of your Mac (or the one you pick in Settings, General). The translations were made by AI: if a word sounds wrong, you can fix it. - **What's new, in the island**: once after the update, the island opens on what Col 3 brings, tile after tile. - **Since 2.0**, in short (each version has its own notes below): the wings are made for macOS 27 and never cover the » button, a menu or an icon; screens without a notch get a pill in the menu bar (2.1). Lyrics on the Lock Screen and on the desktop, word by word, and bars that follow the real sound (2.2). Weather, your next meeting, a microphone mute, your accessories' batteries, Pomodoro and tools for the shelf (2.3). Col Connect for your phone and your home, widgets from anywhere, and Claude Code's questions and plans answered from the island (2.4).

- **Col Connect**: your iPhone, Home Assistant, a Raspberry Pi or a build machine on your network can now push live activities and widgets into the island. Turn it on in Settings, Connect, pair each device (a QR code for your phone, a token for the others), and it reaches the same routes as `colctl`. Each device has its own token, kept in your Keychain, which you can replace or take back; the list says when each one was last seen. Off until you turn it on, it answers only your local network, and Allow and Deny for your agents never leave the Mac. The guide has a ready Shortcut, curl and Home Assistant: [docs/connect.md](docs/connect.md). - **Widgets**: a new Widgets place for your pages shows small cards with a figure, a bar, a few lines and up to three buttons, pushed by `colctl widget set`, the local API, Col Connect or an extension, in one documented format. A widget dims when its figures are old, and can also show beside the camera. A widget's button calls its address only once you have said yes to it, the host shown on its own. - **Widgets from any web address**: in Settings, Connect, give an address that answers JSON, pick what each field shows with key paths such as `{data.temp}`, and see the widget as you type. Col reads it at the interval you choose, and only while the widget shows. Tokens for its headers stay in your Keychain and never go to another host. - **Plans to review**: when Claude Code asks to leave plan mode, the island shows the plan itself, as Markdown you can scroll and select, with Approve and Keep Planning. - **Questions in the island**: when Claude Code asks you a question, the island shows it with its options. Click one to answer, or answer in the terminal, which comes forward. - **Back to the terminal**: click an agent's session in the island and its own tab comes forward in Terminal or iTerm2, or its folder's window in VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf or Zed. macOS asks once to let Col select the tab. - **More extensions**: Countdown, Homebrew Outdated, Docker Containers and Website Status join the examples, and `colctl extensions install` checks an extension's manifest and copies it in from a folder or a repository, turned off until you have read it.

- **The weather**: now, today's high and low and the next hours, with the sky drawn by SF Symbols, in a Weather widget you can put on any page, and beside the clock of the Lock Screen when the island shows there. Where you are, or in a city you type. It comes from Open-Meteo, which needs no account: Col sends it a position rounded to about a kilometre, at most every 30 minutes and only while the weather shows. Off until you turn it on in Settings, Weather and tools. - **Your next meeting**: a few minutes before an event, a countdown in its calendar's colour beside the camera, then "Now" as it starts, and Join on the Live page when the event has a call link. Five minutes by default, from one to thirty (Settings, Live activities). It takes its place in the order you give the closed island. - **Mute your microphone from the island**: a Mute button on the Live page while an app listens mutes your Mac's default microphone, and the closed island shows a red microphone as long as it stays muted. Unmuting gives back the very microphone Col muted, at the level it had, even if another one has become the default; turning the setting off or quitting Col unmutes it too. If you like, ⌃⌥⌘M does the same from any app (Settings, Shortcuts and gestures). - **Caps Lock and the keyboard backlight**: Caps Lock on or off for a moment, if you turn it on, and the keyboard backlight's level as you press its keys, like volume and brightness. The backlight follows your choice for the volume and brightness displays. - **Your accessories' batteries**: a Devices widget shows your mouse, keyboard, trackpad and game controller with their battery, and the island says so when one falls under 15 %. - **Pomodoro**: focus, then a break, counted in the wings like the timer, with a gentle sound when each ends and today's sessions counted. In the Tools page beside the timer, or as a widget. 25 and 5 minutes, or your own. - **Tools for files on the shelf**: from a file's menu, convert an image to PNG, JPEG or HEIC, halve it or bring a Retina capture to 1x, compress files into a .zip, or copy the text of an image. Everything runs on your Mac, and what the tools make lands beside the original and on the shelf, under a name of its own: never over another file. - **Search your copies**: a search field above the clipboard history finds a copy by its words or the app it came from. The island takes the keyboard only while you type, and Return copies the first match. - **The graphics processor** on the System page, beside the processor, measured only while you look. - **Keys let go as they should**: when Col shows the volume or brightness, the key's release now always reaches macOS, so Control Center and other apps no longer wait for it.

- **Lyrics on the Lock Screen**: while the Mac is locked and music plays, the lyrics show large under the clock, the line being sung bright, the one before and the ones to come dim around it, each line gliding into place as the song moves on. Long instrumental passages breathe three dots. The cover, blurred and darkened, sits behind the words so they read on any wallpaper (a deep shade of its colour with Reduce Transparency), and the controls stay at the foot. The lyrics keep between the clock and your picture, never over the password field. Settings, Music and lyrics; it relies on Show on the Lock Screen, and so on private macOS functions. - **The Lock Screen on recent macOS**: Col read the number of its Lock Screen space in half the room macOS gives it, which kept the widgets off the Lock Screen on recent versions; it now reads it whole. If macOS one day lacks what the feature needs, Settings says so instead of offering a switch that does nothing. - **Lyrics on the desktop**: the line being sung, large, with the next one smaller below it, above your wallpaper and below your icons and every window, in the centre or lower left, centre or right, in three sizes. Clicks go through it, it never takes the focus, it shows only while music plays with synced lyrics, and it fades away a few seconds after a pause. It follows Hide the island from screenshots and recordings. Off by default; Settings, Music and lyrics. - **Word by word**: lyrics timed word by word fill as they are sung, from left to right, in the island, on the Lock Screen and on the desktop. A word sung in several pieces fills as one word, and lyrics written without spaces fill piece by piece. With Reduce Motion, each word lights up whole. Lyrics timed line by line show as before. - **Lyrics that are off**: a ⋯ button on the lyrics in the island shows them half a second sooner or later at a time, until they meet the voice, or back on time. Not the right lyrics? Choose among the other recordings LRCLIB has for the song, synced ones first, with their length and album. Or hide the lyrics of that song. Each choice is kept for that song only, everywhere its lyrics show; hidden songs are listed in Settings, Music and lyrics, to show them again. Choosing asks LRCLIB with the same title and artist as before, and nothing else. - **Bars that follow the sound**: the bars beside the camera can move with the music itself, and a small spectrum joins the player in the open island. Col listens to the player's sound (or the Mac's, when the player's own cannot be told apart) and analyses it as it plays: nothing is recorded, kept or sent. The bars listen only while they show and music plays, and use about 1.5 % of one core then. macOS asks for System Audio Recording when you turn it on, and only then; until you allow it, the bars dance on their own, as before. Off by default; Settings, Music and lyrics. Needs macOS 14.2 or later. - **When Col cannot see the menu bar**: without Device Control and Data Access (Accessibility before macOS 27), Col cannot tell where the menus and icons are. The wings now stay narrow then, room for an icon, instead of reaching over what they cannot see, and the island says so once, with a button that opens the right place in System Settings.

- **Made for macOS 27**: macOS 27 draws every menu bar icon in one place and puts its own » button for hidden icons right beside the notch. Col now watches that menu bar and measures it again the moment an icon comes or goes, so its wings never cover the » button, an icon or a menu. The wings also leave room for the island's rounded edges and for its swell under the pointer, which used to reach a few points over the first icon. When there is no room on one side, the activity keeps a single wing on the other; a line of text too long for that wing gives way to its icon. - **A pill on screens without a notch**: on an external display or a Mac without a notch, the island is now a small black pill inside the menu bar, clear of the top edge, the way the iPhone's island sits in its status bar. It stretches to show what is happening and opens into a card with four round corners. Prefer Col's notch, or the larger capsule below the menu bar? Settings, Appearance, Shape. Turn off "Show the island when nothing happens" to see it only when something happens. When an app's menus reach the middle of the menu bar, the pill steps out of their way. - **Below the menu bar, even with a notch**: on a Mac whose notch area already shows something, such as its own Dynamic Island, the island can float below the menu bar instead (Settings, Appearance, Shape). - **Wings as wide as you like**: choose how far the closed island may reach beside the camera, Narrow, Standard or Wide (Settings, Appearance, Shape). Whatever the choice, it never covers a menu or an icon. - **Long lines glide**: a song title or a lyric too long for its wing glides across it, held still at each end, instead of ending with an ellipsis. With Reduce Motion, it still ends with an ellipsis. - **Step aside for some apps**: choose apps in front of which the island hides, as it does in full screen (Settings, General). Volume, alerts and requests still show. - **Open and close from a link**: `col://open`, `col://open?page=live` and `col://close`, for Shortcuts and scripts. - **macOS 27 names**: the permission Col asks for its wings and its volume display is called Device Control and Data Access on macOS 27, and Col now says so.

- **Islet is now Col**: the same app under a shorter name. A col is the pass between two peaks, and the notch is one. The update takes care of everything: the app takes its new name in Applications, and your settings, permissions, pages and extensions stay as they were. `islet://` links, the `islet` command and the hooks your agents already call keep working; in a terminal, the command is now `colctl`, since macOS already has a `col`. If you installed Islet with Homebrew, the app keeps its old name so Homebrew can still upgrade and remove it, and `brew upgrade --cask --greedy col` gives you Col.app. The icon and the website now light the notch in macOS blue. - **New settings**: a bigger window that opens below the island instead of under it, grouped panes with a search field, and headers that stay put while the settings scroll beneath them. Appearance and Pages show your own island, drawn by Col itself on your wallpaper with what it shows right now, and every change of size or glass also plays on the notch. While the settings are open, Col has a Dock icon and menus, so ⌘Tab, copy and paste work as anywhere. - **Synced lyrics**: the words of the song beside the player, line by line, the way Apple Music shows them, whatever plays (Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, your browser). Tap a line to jump there; long instrumental passages breathe three dots. Optionally, the line being sung in the closed island. Lyrics come from LRCLIB, an open database: only the title, the artist, the album and the length of the track are sent, and the answer is kept on your Mac. Your own `.lrc` files take precedence. Settings, Music and lyrics. Lyrics are on in a new install, where the welcome shows the choice; after an update from Islet they stay off until you turn them on. - **The prompter, in the notch**: Souffleur joins Col. Your script comes out of the notch right under the camera and rolls at the pace of your voice: it waits when you stop talking (Voice Pace), follows your words one by one (Voice Follow), rolls at a steady pace, or moves only when you move it. It lives on a page of the island with its play button, has its own Scripts window and its own pane in Settings, and stays out of screenshots, recordings and calls. While it is out, the island steps aside and comes back after the take. Drive it with ⌃⌥⌘P and its other shortcuts, a presentation clicker, your phone, Shortcuts actions or `col://prompter/…` links. If you used Souffleur, your scripts and settings carry over, and its `souffleur://` links keep working. Your phone stays paired, and its remote waits until you turn it on in Settings, Prompter. Souffleur itself, still open beside Col, is asked to quit so that your shortcuts drive only one prompter, and the island says once that it can go to the Trash. - **Pages you compose**: each page of the open island holds one widget across it or two side by side, and each place can stack several widgets: the island shows the first one that has something to show. Home now puts the player beside the song's lyrics, and the clock beside your agenda while nothing plays. Add, rename, reorder and remove pages in Settings, Pages, where the island shows the page as you edit it. Your pages from Islet 1 carry over, and the AI and prompter pages join them. - **What the closed island shows first**: when several things run at once, the order is yours (Settings, Live activities). Volume, brightness, alerts and requests still come first. - **AI apps, all of them**: Col recognizes the AI apps on your Mac (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Grok Bot, Cursor, VS Code, Zed, Ollama, LM Studio and more) with their own icons, and shows the open ones on an AI page of the island, a tap away. Add your own AI: an Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or OpenAI-compatible server on this Mac or on another machine of your network; the island shows whether it answers, the model it holds and, when the server can tell, whether it is generating. Tokens stay in your Keychain. Settings, AI apps. - **Ask your AI from the island**: a field at the foot of the AI page asks the model you pick on your own servers (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, OpenAI-compatible). The answer comes as the model writes it, Markdown included, with its thinking aloud kept out of sight; follow up, copy the answer, or start over. The island takes the keyboard only while you type, as Spotlight does. Questions go to that server only and the conversation is never written to disk. - **Agents show their logo**: Claude Code shows Claude's logo, and Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and GitHub Copilot theirs, in the closed island, on the Live page, on the AI page and in the settings. The icon of the app installed when there is one, else the brand's own logo, which Col carries. When an agent starts waiting for you, its logo hops a few times, as in the Dock, then rests (not with Reduce Motion). Each icon is kept only at the size it shows. - **The whole command before you allow it**: when an agent asks to run a command, the Allow card shows it in full, in a fixed-width font you can scroll and select, with spaces, tabs and line breaks made visible. A command too long to check there cannot be allowed from the island: the card asks you to answer in the terminal. - **More pages fit**: six tabs fit beside the camera; with more pages, the tabs become dots, as on the iPhone. - **Permissions**: one pane says what each permission is for, which feature needs it, and when Reminders and Local Network are asked. - **Extensions keep to their own permissions**: an extension's script no longer inherits Col's Accessibility, Microphone, Camera or Calendars permissions; macOS treats it as a program of its own. Extensions still run on their schedule, as before. - **Shortcuts and gestures**: every way to open and drive the island, in one place. - **Language**: Col follows the language of your Mac, or the one you pick in Settings, General. - **Your Mac's accent colour**: buttons, switches, selections and what is on take the accent colour chosen in System Settings, Appearance, as in Apple's apps, instead of Col's coral. Settings panes keep fixed colours, as in System Settings. The prompter's stage light follows the accent too, unless you pick another. - **A welcome made for your Mac**: Col looks at what the Mac has and starts from there: the song playing with its cover, the music apps, the headphones connected, the battery, the AI apps and coding agents with their logos (connect each agent in one click), your next event once you allow the calendars. Each feature starts on when the Mac has what it needs, and a permission is asked on the line that needs it, its result shown at once. Then your island, with the pages your choices make, plays on your own wallpaper with what is really happening, and an example of an agent asking for permission. - **A first hello in every language**: on first launch the island says hello in your Mac's language, even one Col does not speak yet, then in others, from Japanese to Arabic, each word giving way to the next in a soft blur, and back to yours. The welcome window is born out of the island, and at the end goes back into the notch while the island says "Let's go". With Reduce Motion, simple fades. - **One island**: a second copy of Col, opened from Downloads or from a build folder, hands over to the one already running instead of drawing a second island and taking its connection to your agents. - **Long lines beside the camera**: a line too long for its wing, a song's title or the lyric being sung, showed nothing at all. It now ends with an ellipsis.

- **GitHub Copilot in VS Code**, contributed by [@BonnetAdam](https://github.com/BonnetAdam): Copilot's agent sessions show in the notch like the other agents, with the project, the tool it runs, and Done when an answer is complete, through VS Code's own hooks. Connect it in Settings, Developers, or with `islet hooks install --agent copilot`. Islet only watches: VS Code keeps each session's own permission mode. - **Agents**: each has its own symbol in the notch (Claude Code keeps the sparkle), and two permission requests from one session no longer cancel each other (also by @BonnetAdam). A request answered in the terminal leaves the island once its tool has run.

- **Liquid Glass**: on macOS 26, the open island stays black where it meets the notch and melts into glass toward its lower edge, so it sits on your desktop instead of covering it. Choose it in Settings, Island, Liquid Glass, as macOS lets you choose for its own glass: Liquid (the default: clear glass that magnifies and bends what lies behind it along its edges, like a thick pane), Transparent (the desktop seen through, lightly blurred and dimmed), Tinted (Apple's frosted Liquid Glass) or Black. It stays black when Reduce transparency is on. - **Fixed**: the battery percentage no longer breaks over two lines when the Live tab shares the top bar.

The first release of Islet: a Dynamic Island for the MacBook notch, free and open source under the MIT License.
- **Now playing**: artwork, scrubber, controls and output picker in the island; the track peeks in the wings when it changes, and a swipe on the closed island skips it. - **AI agents**: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor sessions show in the notch while they work; Claude Code's and Codex's permission requests get Allow and Deny buttons. No account, no login: connect each agent in one click from Settings. Any other agent or script reports with `islet agent`. - **Programmable**: an `islet` command, a local API, an `islet://` URL scheme and Shortcuts actions push your own live activities; extensions add more. - **Privacy**: a green or orange light when the camera or the microphone is in use, and which app is using it. - **Every Mac**: on displays without a notch, Islet floats under the menu bar. It never covers a menu or a menu bar icon: when an app's menus reach the notch, the activity keeps a single wing on the free side. - **AirPods, by model**: AirPods, AirPods Pro, AirPods Max and Beats recognised from the model they report, each with its own card and battery. - **The rest of the island**: headphone battery, volume and brightness, charging, a shelf for files, clipboard history with pins, agenda and reminders, timers, a mirror, a color picker, system stats, keep awake, downloads. - **Settings and onboarding**: turn each module on or off, reorder the pages, choose the size and the motion, and meet Islet in a short guided tour that asks only for the permissions your modules need. - **Updates**: Islet checks for updates with Sparkle; every update is EdDSA-signed and notarized by Apple.
